AAON_2023q1.summary_analysis: AAON reported record fourth-quarter 2022 sales, gross margin, earnings and backlog, and the Motley Fool reported that AAON shares rose 19.2% in February, a move it said came mainly from this 'excellent set of fourth-quarter 2022 earnings.' Net sales rose 86.8% to a record $254.6 million, gross margin expanded to 30.8% of sales, and diluted EPS jumped to $0.71 from $0.11, while backlog grew 110.6% to a record $548.0 million on robust order intake. The Motley Fool tied the rally to results that dispelled investor fears about AAON's trading conditions, citing the company's lighter exposure to a weakening residential HVAC market relative to peers Carrier and Trane, and management struck an optimistic tone entering 2023 after a slow start to the prior year.
AAON_2023q1.explicit_reasons: The Motley Fool explicitly attributed AAON shares' 19.2% rise in February mainly to an 'excellent set of fourth-quarter 2022 earnings.' Within that report, net sales grew 86.8% year-over-year to a record $254.6 million, gross margin expanded to 30.8% of sales with diluted EPS up to $0.71 from $0.11, and backlog reached a record $548.0 million, up 110.6% year-over-year with orders outpacing both the prior and year-ago quarters -- results the article credited, together with the easing of fears about AAON's trading conditions, as drivers of the rally.
AAON_2023q1.implicit_reasons: The Motley Fool noted AAON's comparatively light exposure to the weakening residential HVAC market -- in contrast to peers Carrier and Trane, whose residential orders fell roughly 30% and in the mid-20% range, respectively -- as context that helped ease investor fears about AAON's trading conditions, adding to the positive sentiment, even while cautioning that a protracted housing downturn could eventually weigh on AAON's commercial markets. Management also struck an optimistic tone for 2023, with the CEO saying the company was positioned for 'another record year of sales and earnings' after 2022 started slowly but finished with record results and an improved backlog margin profile; the articles give no specific figure for this outlook.

Guidance.text: Management said it was optimistic AAON was positioned for 'another record year of sales and earnings' in 2023, after 2022 started slowly but finished with record sales, EBITDA and earnings and a backlog with an improved margin profile; the articles give no specific figure for this outlook, only management's more confident tone.

Order book / backlog.text: Backlog closed the fourth quarter at a record $548.0 million, up 110.6% from $260.2 million a year earlier, with orders outpacing both the prior and year-ago quarters. The Motley Fool called this a 'whopping' gain and, alongside the rest of the 'excellent' report, tied it to the stock's 19.2% rise in February and the easing of fears about AAON's trading conditions.

The Motley Fool said this result was part of the 'excellent' earnings report that dispelled investor fears about AAON's trading conditions and drove the stock's 19.2% rise in February.

Profits, costs and margin.text: Gross margin expanded to 30.8% of sales from a supply-chain-constrained year-earlier quarter, and diluted EPS rose to $0.71 from $0.11. The Motley Fool credited this profitability improvement, part of an 'excellent' quarter that eased fears about AAON's trading conditions, as a driver of the shares' 19.2% rise in February.

Macro and micro development.text: The Motley Fool noted AAON's comparatively light exposure to the weakening residential HVAC market compared with peers Carrier, whose residential orders fell roughly 30%, and Trane, whose residential bookings fell in the mid-20% range, framing this as part of what eased investor fears about AAON's trading conditions, while cautioning a protracted housing downturn could eventually weigh on AAON's commercial markets.

AAON_2024q1.summary_analysis: AAON reported record fourth-quarter 2023 sales, margin and earnings alongside growing bookings, and Zacks reported that the stock rose on the results, titling its report 'AAON's Stock Rises on Q4 Earnings Beat, Bookings Up Y/Y.' Net sales grew 20.4% to a record $306.6 million, gross margin expanded to 36.4% from 30.8%, and diluted EPS rose 19.1% to $0.56, while bookings increased for a second straight quarter, lifting backlog 4.0% sequentially to $510.0 million. Management struck a cautiously optimistic tone for 2024, citing continued but slower sales and earnings growth amid signs of a slowing nonresidential construction market and uncertainty around an industry refrigerant transition.
AAON_2024q1.explicit_reasons: Zacks explicitly tied AAON's stock rise to the fourth-quarter results, titling its report 'AAON's Stock Rises on Q4 Earnings Beat, Bookings Up Y/Y.'
